items.reason: Added a judge eval corpus (crates/engine/evals/judge/corpus.json) of seven cases with whole recorded verdicts — overall, pass, per-dimension score and floor_hit, agreement, parse accounting, injection signal — plus pinned judge-prompt phrases, replayed through the real prompt/scorer/aggregate path with the provider call canned; it runs inside the blocking cargo test --workspace gate and is declared as the judge-eval capability in .ai/manifest.yaml and run by scripts/gates.sh.

Added .github/CODEOWNERS (global owner plus the store/engine/contract/workflow/deploy seams) and a second pre-commit rung that runs cargo fmt --all -- --check -l and fails the commit only when one of the author's staged .rs files is in the rewrite list; documented both in CONTRIBUTING.md, with LIGHTTRACK_SKIP_FMT=1 as the deliberate bypass and an announced skip when cargo is absent.

The OpenAPI half was already covered another way and left alone — crates/api/src/openapi.rs serves /openapi.json rendered from lighttrack-contract, clients/contract/openapi.baseline.json is the committed published baseline, and a removal guard fails the build when a name leaves the surface unmarked; the missing half, CHANGELOG.md, now exists in Keep-a-Changelog form with an Unreleased section, and the PR template asks for an entry (or an explicit N/A) so entries are written while the change is fresh.

Needs write access to .claude/CLAUDE.md, which this session's harness refuses as a sensitive path: the scaffold text (npm run build / npm run test / 'Add your project description here') is still there and only rewriting that file removes it, so a human must replace its body with a stub pointing at root CLAUDE.md; what could be done without touching it was done — .ai/manifest.yaml now declares guidance.canonical: CLAUDE.md with .claude/CLAUDE.md listed under staleProjections, and root CLAUDE.md declares itself canonical and names the stale file, so a reader now knows which document to disbelieve.

Needs network: pinning the 29 Action references requires asking GitHub what each floating tag points at right now, and inventing a SHA breaks a workflow rather than pinning it — so all 29 remain unpinned and the next scan will still see that; the signing/SBOM half of the item was implemented (keyless cosign sign-blob plus an SPDX SBOM in a separate release.yml job that runs after the artifacts are attached, cosign sign + spdxjson attestation over the pushed manifest digest at the end of docker.yml's merge job, and verification commands in SECURITY.md), but those steps are unverified because this session cannot run CI.

lessons: This repository already answers most process gaps with a guard test rather than a document: crates/core/tests/{manifest_guard,gate_table_guard,catchup_marker_guard,chart_policy_guard}.rs each fail cargo test --workspace when a projection drifts from its authority. Before adding a new practice here, check whether an existing guard already covers it, and add the new one in the same shape — .ai/manifest.yaml is the authority for commands, .github/workflows/ci.yml for what blocks, and both are mechanically bound to scripts/gates.sh and CONTRIBUTING.md's gate table, so adding a blocking capability without updating gates.sh (and a CI job without a CONTRIBUTING table row) turns the suite red.

Scan findings here can be stale in both directions: this cycle's 'no OpenAPI spec' gap was already closed by a served /openapi.json plus a 400 kB committed baseline and a deprecation removal guard, and 'nothing catches a violation before push' understated an existing .githooks/pre-push that runs every blocking gate. Read the repo before writing; the real gap is usually narrower and more specific than the item states.

An Ascent session in this environment cannot write under .claude/ — the harness classifies it as a sensitive path and refuses both Write and Edit. Items whose fix is 'rewrite .claude/CLAUDE.md' cannot be closed by an agent here and should be routed to a human, or the guidance-canonical pointer should live somewhere writable (.ai/manifest.yaml works).
